name: 12-3-30 incline walking

lead: The 12-3-30 workout is a treadmill routine: a 12 percent incline, 3 miles per hour, 30 minutes of walking. It spread through social media and is used as a low-impact way to burn extra calories and lose fat for a leaner physique.

Walking on a steep incline raises the effort of walking without the impact of running. Published research is limited: a 2025 exploratory study in the International Journal of Exercise Science compared its metabolic responses with self-paced treadmill running.

paras: Users set the treadmill to 12 percent incline and 3 mph and walk for 30 minutes, often several times a week, sometimes as a warm-up or after lifting.
Generally considered low-risk; steep inclines can strain calves or ankles for some people.

angle.text: A steep 12% incline walk burns extra calories without the joint impact of running, supporting fat loss and a leaner physique. A small exploratory 2025 study has looked at its metabolic responses.

lead: The 12-3-30 workout is a treadmill routine named for its settings: a 12 percent incline, a speed of 3 miles per hour and 30 minutes of walking. People use it to burn calories and lean out, which makes the face and body look more defined, as a low-impact alternative to running. It spread through social media and is discussed in looksmaxxing and fitness circles as a fat-loss routine.[1][2]

Wikipedia credits the routine to social media creator Lauren Giraldo, who says she settled on the settings in 2017 while trying to focus on her health and did it five times a week; her November 2020 TikTok about it went viral, and the hashtag later passed 131 million views.[2]

Published research is limited. A 2025 exploratory study in the International Journal of Exercise Science, with 16 participants, compared the workout with self-paced treadmill running when both were matched for total energy expenditure. Walking took longer, burned energy at a lower rate and used a higher share of fat and lower share of carbohydrate as fuel.[1]

paras: The routine is done on a treadmill set to the maximum or near-maximum incline most home machines allow, at a walking pace, without holding the rails in the usual version shown online. Its appeal is simplicity: one fixed setting, a fixed duration and no running.[2]

Giraldo has said she tried different treadmill settings in 2017 and chose these three numbers, then promoted the routine on her channels.[2] Her November 2020 TikTok brought it to wide attention and other influencers began posting their own versions, with the #12330workout hashtag reaching about 131 million views.[2] Media coverage such as Washington Post and Fortune pieces asked whether it is healthy and whether it works.[2]

In the 2025 study, sixteen participants (seven women, nine men) completed both sessions in a laboratory with a metabolic analyzer. When total energy expenditure was matched, 12-3-30 took longer, had a lower rate of energy expenditure, a higher percentage of fat use and a lower percentage of carbohydrate use than self-paced running.[1] The authors wrote that it may be less time-efficient for expending energy but may suit people aiming to increase fat utilization.[1]

One exploratory crossover-style laboratory study published in 2025 compared the metabolic responses of 12-3-30 with self-paced treadmill running in 16 adults.[1] The authors noted that, before it, there were no peer-reviewed studies evaluating the widespread claims about the workout.[1] No trials have been identified that follow people over time to measure body-fat or appearance outcomes.

lore.intro: The routine is circulated as a viral, low-impact alternative to running, and incline walking appears in looksmaxxing and bodybuilding training logs as low-intensity cardio during fat loss.[3]

claims.claim: Incline walking suits fat-loss phases as low-intensity cardio.
